An entry was classified ALREADY_FIXED only when the effective object was a distinct, already-accurate override (verified against the real game); LIVE_CONTAMINATED (-> REPAIRED) when the effective object was still the contaminated base entry itself.

notesForReviewer: Exactly 20 manifest entries were inspected, selected as the next 20 in the manifest's original array order following the 10 already handled by Batch 1.

9 of the 20 were classified ALREADY_FIXED: each already has an accurate, game-specific override from an earlier batch (in every case batch 45) that already supersedes the contaminated base shelfcheck-dossiers.txt entry at runtime. Josh has never actually seen the contaminated text for any of these 9. Each was independently re-verified against the real game for accuracy and deliberately left untouched -- no research-for-its-own-sake rewrites were performed, per the batch-1 lesson.

11 of the 20 were classified REPAIRED (genuinely LIVE_CONTAMINATED): no override existed, so the contaminated base text was what ShelfCheck actually served. New, game-specific overrides for these 11 were added in a new file, dossier-overrides-47.js, following the exact same {t,s,w,c,r,b,p} object-literal schema as every prior batch.

Bibi & Tina at the horse farm's dossier text is now accurate about the actual game while explicitly noting it remains excluded from the Josh Set (HORSE_GAME, curation pass #1) -- this repair only touched dossier content, not census status.

dossier-apply.js, index.html, and sw.js each received exactly one minimal line-edit to register/precache the new batch file, consistent with every prior batch; sw.js's cache generation was bumped shelfcheck-v136 -> shelfcheck-v137.
